hook.text: Oxygen turns fats rancid. Antioxidant preservatives sacrifice themselves to protect your food from going bad.

buildup.text: Rancidity produces off-flavors and toxic compounds. Oils, chips, and cereals are all vulnerable to oxidation.

discovery.text: BHA and BHT donate hydrogen atoms to free radicals, breaking the chain reaction that causes rancidity.

twist.text: BHA is 'possibly carcinogenic' in animal studies. Yet it's still widely used because human evidence is weak.

climax.text: Rosemary extract and vitamin E are natural antioxidant alternatives now replacing BHA and BHT in many products.

punchline.text: Antioxidants in food aren't health boosters. They're bodyguards for fat.

quiz.question: How do antioxidant preservatives like BHA and BHT work?
options: They donate hydrogen atoms to free radicals, stopping oxidation chain reactions
